name: rocket-form-path-aliases
instr:
Please add nested wire-name aliases to Rocket's `rocket::form::FromForm` derive so a form can use a name such as `account.contact.email` without requiring intermediate Rust structs. Work in `/app` and don't add new crates.

A named field accepts `#[field(path = "account.contact.email")]` or `#[field(path = uncased("Account.Contact.Email"))]`. Paths use Rocket's form-name key syntax: dots and brackets separate keys, while a dot inside brackets belongs to that key. An uncased path matches every key case-insensitively. Like `name`, `path` can be repeated, and both can appear on the same field; specifying either replaces the implicit Rust field-name alias.

Match aliases against the current position in the incoming name and send the remaining keys to the field's `FromForm` implementation. Among all matching aliases, the one consuming the most keys wins, regardless of field order; equal-length matches go to the first declared field. This choice happens before parsing, with no retry of a shorter alias on a parse error. Apply the same rules to value and data fields. For example, with fields aliased to `cfg` and `cfg.mode`, `cfg[mode]=17` belongs to the latter, while `cfg.other=x` belongs to the former with `other` left for its parser.
